OctoLab - Science Beneath Every Tentacle, OctoLab is a documentary channel driven by scientific curiosity and a deep fascination with the natural world.

At OctoLab, we explore science, animals, and the hidden intelligence of nature — from extraordinary animal behavior to the biological systems that shape life on Earth. Complex scientific ideas are presented through clear, engaging storytelling designed to inform, inspire, and spark curiosity.

Guided by Dr. Octopus, OctoLab invites you to look beyond appearances and understand how the natural world truly functions.

chi_tiet.tieu_de: The Way Orcas Prepare for Death Has Shocked the World
chi_tiet.mo_ta:
The Way Orcas Prepare for Death Has Shocked the World explores a side of killer whales that is rarely seen: how they respond when a family member is dying or already gone.

In The Way Orcas Prepare for Death Has Shocked the World, we look at remarkable cases where pod members supported weakened whales at the surface, shared food with injured individuals, and remained beside dead calves for days. Stories like Hunchy and Tahlequah reveal just how deeply orca survival depends on family bonds, shared knowledge, and long-term social connections.

But death does not end with the pod. When a killer whale sinks to the seafloor, its body can become a whale fall, feeding deep-sea organisms and supporting new life.

Ultimately, The Way Orcas Prepare for Death Has Shocked the World reveals that for orcas, death is not simply disappearance—it becomes part of both their social legacy and the larger cycle of the ocean.

chi_tiet.tieu_de: Why The Entire Ocean is Terrified of Pilot Whales
chi_tiet.mo_ta:
Why The Entire Ocean is Terrified of Pilot Whales explores one of the ocean’s strangest rivalries: why even killer whales sometimes abandon hunts when pilot whales arrive.

In Why The Entire Ocean is Terrified of Pilot Whales, we uncover how enormous super-pods use aggressive mobbing, overwhelming numbers, and constant acoustic communication to pressure predators far stronger than any individual pilot whale.

Their greatest weapon isn’t teeth or raw strength—it’s unity. By moving and responding as a single group, pilot whales can turn even an apex predator’s hunt into a dangerous risk.

Ultimately, Why The Entire Ocean is Terrified of Pilot Whales reveals why, in the ocean, the strongest predator does not always control the battlefield.
